key_insight: Instead of giving each transformer layer its own expert set, UniPool shares a single, global pool of experts across layers—showing that much of per-layer expert isolation is unnecessary and expert capacity can be reused with minimal accuracy loss.
problem_solved: Breaks the rigid per-layer expert allocation in Mixture-of-Experts models, which couples depth scaling to linear growth in expert parameters and wastes capacity by assuming every layer needs isolated experts.
method: Introduce a globally shared expert pool that all transformer layers can access, decoupling expert count from model depth.
Design lightweight routing and access controls so layers select experts from the shared pool while maintaining load balance and training stability.
Empirically validate with routing probes showing uniform/random routing causes only small downstream accuracy drops, motivating shared expert reuse.
impact: UniPool reduces expert-parameter bloat and improves parameter efficiency for large sparse models, making MoE scaling cheaper and simpler for practitioners without sacrificing much accuracy.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: per-layer experts (many isolated boxes) vs UniPool (one central pool with multi-layer access arrows).
Bar chart: expert-parameter count and total params for traditional MoE vs UniPool at increasing depths.
Line plot: accuracy vs. expert count showing small accuracy drop when using shared pool or random routing.
Icon set: scalability (stacked blocks), efficiency (leaf/gear), and robustness (shield) to summarize benefits.
paper_title: UniPool: A Globally Shared Expert Pool for Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Minbin Huang, Han Shi, Chuanyang Zheng, Yimeng Wu, Guoxuan Chen
